subject: Retention & Deletion Evidence — BrightOak pilot 90d exception?
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@brightoakdx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 13:22:00 -0400
Subject: Request: retention/deletion evidence for SIG/CAIQ — BrightOak pilot

Hi Marissa / Kimberly,

We're preparing BrightOak's vendor SIG/CAIQ submission for an upcoming internal audit and need a few artifacts related to data retention and deletion specific to the pilot we're running with Redwood. The compliance team has three discrete asks: 

1) A retention matrix that maps customer data classes (session traces, inference logs, debug dumps, embeddings) to retention windows and deletion mechanisms.
2) A concise description of the deletion workflow (who/what triggers deletion, how deletion is verified, time-to-delete SLA).
3) Any documented exceptions or process for customer-specific retention carve-outs (we are evaluating a 90-day pilot for aggregated diagnostic traces).

Could you share the artifacts and a short point person for a follow-up call? We need to deliver the SIG/CAIQ pack by next Friday.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Dawson
Security & Privacy, BrightOak Diagnostics

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention/deletion evidence for SIG/CAIQ — BrightOak pilot

Hi Claire / Marissa — attaching the retention matrix as discussed. Highlights below, extracted from the attached spreadsheet: 

- Session traces (non-PII): default 30 days; automated TTL-based deletion via object lifecycle rules; deletion job runs nightly and reports to SIEM.
- Inference logs (request/response pairs with PII redaction markers): 90 days for audit-enabled accounts; default 30 days otherwise; deletion handled via job that marks records as tombstoned and then purges after verification.
- Debug dumps (ephemeral stacks): default 7 days; ephemeral by design, stored encrypted in a limited-access bucket; auto-purge at 7 days.
- Embeddings (hashed): retained 365 days unless customer requests earlier deletion; deletion requires data disposal ticket and backend verification.

Deletion verification: each deletion job emits a signed artifact (delete_manifest.json) to an internal artifact store. We produce periodic proofs for SOC2/CAIQ sample requests. Time-to-delete SLA: bulk purge complete within 48 hours of approved deletion ticket; tombstone-to-final-delete within configured TTL window (24–72 hours depending on workload).

Attached: retention_matrix_QA.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78 KB)

Let me know if you need an export sample (small) from a tenant; we can redact and provide a sanitized audit log snippet.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Engineering — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retention_matrix_QA.xlsx]

From: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@brightoakdx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:31:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention/deletion evidence for SIG/CAIQ — BrightOak pilot

Thanks Kim — that matrix is very helpful. Two clarifications before we finalize our submission: 

1) For debug dumps: can you confirm the deletion verification artifact format and retention of those artifacts? We need to show proof of delete for the CAIQ sample.
2) Regarding the 90-day pilot: BrightOak's product team is proposing a pilot where aggregated, de-identified diagnostic traces will be retained for 90 days (instead of 30) for analytics. This data contains no PII but would have longer life. What controls/compensating measures would Redwood require to approve a customer-specific retention carve-out?

I've attached a small redacted sample of an audit-log stanza for reference.

[Attachment: audit_log_sample_snippet.txt]

Appreciate a short write-up so we can include it in the SIG packet. Also please propose a short MoA (mutual action plan) and any contract change language for the pilot.

—Claire

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@brightoakdx.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention/deletion evidence for SIG/CAIQ — BrightOak pilot

Claire — quick summary and next steps below (happy to jump on a call this week to finalize wording).

1) Debug dumps / verification artifacts:
- Format: delete_manifest.json (name, object-key, deletion-timestamp, SHA256 of deleted object, digital signature from Redwood KMS).
- Retention of artifacts: delete_manifest entries are stored for 365 days and are searchable via our evidence portal. We can export redacted manifests for CAIQ/SIG samples.

2) 90-day pilot (aggregated, de-identified diagnostic traces) — proposed compensating controls:
- Data must be pre-processed by BrightOak to strip any PII before ingestion to Redwood. BrightOak must provide the preprocessing checklist and test evidence.
- Enhanced access controls: restrict dataset to a dedicated Redwood tenant with role-based access; require MFA + session recording for any admin access.
- Monitoring: enabled audit logging for all read/write/delete operations; daily integrity checks comparing object store and delete manifests.
- Contractual: limited-time exception (90 days) documented in an MoA; mutual termination clause for the pilot and requirement to confirm deletion at pilot end.

If that is acceptable we will: (a) produce a one-page Mutual Action Plan (attached) for signature, (b) add a short rider to the SOW referencing the 90-day exception and compensating controls, and (c) provide a sanitized delete_manifest export for your SIG pack.

Attachments: pilot_mutual_action_plan.pdf (14 KB)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbcBrightOakEvidence, HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/BRD-2027-411

Next: If you confirm acceptance of the controls I will get legal and contracts involved and Ben will scope any SOW amendment. Suggested 30-minute call Tuesday 10–10:30 AM ET.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_mutual_action_plan.pdf]
